jobDescription: A podcast and audiobook app recommends episodes and titles on its home screen and in a weekly personalised email. The recommendations team trains retrieval and ranking models, runs online experiments on the in-house experimentation platform and maintains the feature store that serves the models. This engineer will look after model training pipelines, design and analyse A/B tests together with the product analysts and keep model monitoring in place. The effect of a model change is reported only from a controlled experiment with a pre-declared primary metric and test window.
requirements: Trains and maintains retrieval or ranking models for a consumer recommendation surface.
Builds and maintains feature pipelines that publish to a feature store.
Designs online A/B tests with a pre-declared primary metric together with product analysts.
Reports the effect of a model change from a controlled experiment with a defined metric, control group and test window.
Maintains monitoring for model inputs and prediction drift.

evidence.text: Trained a two-tower retrieval model in PyTorch for the home-screen shelf at Tidewater Audio, replacing the earlier popularity-based candidate list.
Wrote Spark jobs that compute listening-history features every hour and publish them to the Feast feature store, with a schema check on each run.
Designed the A/B test plan for the new ranking model with the product analysts, pre-declaring completed-episode starts as the primary metric and a three-week test window.
Set up drift monitoring on the ten most important input features and on the score distribution, with alerts routed to the team channel.
Presented the model architecture and the test plan at the company's monthly machine-learning reading group.

Work sample: the experiment plan for the ranking-model test, listing the hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, the randomisation unit (user account), the sample-size calculation and the three-week window. Its results section is empty because the test was still running when the candidate left.

Reference check summary: Tidewater Audio's former head of data science confirmed by email the candidate's dates of employment (January 2022 to March 2024) and that the candidate trained the two-tower retrieval model described in the resume.

Hiring manager's note after an informal coffee chat: the candidate mentioned that someone on the growth team had estimated the new ranking model 'probably added about 12% to listening time', and that the experiment readout was never shared with the candidate.

propositions.text: The candidate trained a two-tower retrieval model in PyTorch for the home-screen shelf.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the model and the reference check confirms the candidate trained it.

propositions.text: The candidate designed the A/B test plan for the ranking model with a pre-declared primary metric (completed-episode starts) and a three-week window.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the plan and the work sample is the plan document.

propositions.text: The candidate's ranking model increased listening time by about 12%.
propositions.rationale: The figure is a second-hand estimate attributed to an unnamed growth-team member, the candidate never saw the readout, and the plan's results section is empty; under the quantification rule a hearsay figure without a defined baseline is not evidence, and listening time is not the pre-declared metric.

gold.expectedGap: No experiment readout, control-group comparison or test window supports the estimated listening-time effect.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Report the retrieval model, the feature pipeline, the experiment plan and the drift monitoring as documented; record the second-hand listening-time estimate as an unsupported claim with a follow-up about the experiment result.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the ranking-model experiment produced a readout, what the primary-metric result was against control, and over which window.
